title: An Out-of-Window Refund Denial That Turned on Lifetime Spend
scenario_text:
A support lead at Cypressa Retail must decide how to handle an out-of-window goodwill refund request, given how a similar request was handled last month.

**Decision A (2024-06-09)**
Customer 'Petra Alden' requested a goodwill refund 44 days after delivery — outside the standard 30-day refund window. DENIED at the team level. Note: 'Support may issue out-of-window goodwill refunds without manager approval only for customers whose lifetime spend is at least $2,000. Petra's lifetime spend was $610, below the threshold, and no manager approval was obtained. Denied on that basis.'

**Current request C (2024-07-18)**
Customer 'Rowan Beck' requests a goodwill refund 40 days after delivery — also outside the 30-day window. Rowan's lifetime spend is $3,450. The order and account are otherwise ordinary, and Rowan is not claiming a defect; this is a goodwill request.

**Refund Policy (current, unchanged this year)**
Refunds requested within 30 days of delivery are issued automatically once verified. Beyond 30 days, support may issue a one-time goodwill refund WITHOUT manager approval only when the customer's lifetime spend is at least $2,000; below that threshold, an out-of-window goodwill refund requires manager approval and is otherwise declined.

**Slack — #cx-support**
Agent: 'We denied an out-of-window refund just last month, so let's stay consistent and deny Rowan too.'
Lead: 'Hold on — why did we deny that one? Let me check Rowan's lifetime spend before we call it precedent.'

The agent is treating the June denial as a general rule against out-of-window refunds. Rowan's lifetime spend is well above $2,000.
question: How should the lead handle Rowan Beck's out-of-window goodwill refund request?
choices: Deny the refund to stay consistent with the June denial of a comparable out-of-window request.
Approve the goodwill refund at the team level: Rowan's $3,450 lifetime spend clears the $2,000 threshold that the June denial fell below, so support can issue it without manager approval.
Route the request to a manager for approval, given the prior denial of a similar out-of-window request.
Offer store credit instead of a cash refund as a compromise between honoring the request and matching the prior denial.
